plan.title: Case vs control whole-blood DE with effect-size threshold
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a 12,000-gene x 120-sample gene-level count matrix (counts.csv, salmon output as delivered) with a 120-row metadata table carrying one condition column: 60 cases vs 60 controls, unpaired human whole blood, single batch. The research question has two halves — which genes differ, and which differences are large enough to matter — so the plan first establishes sample structure, then fits one test, then answers the effect-size half by testing against a fold-change threshold inside the model rather than filtering a significance list afterwards.

Method choice is driven by the cohort size. With 60 samples per group this is a population-scale cohort, where the negative-binomial count models (DESeq2, edgeR) are documented to exaggerate false positives, including on permuted labels. The plan therefore uses limma-voom with a fixed-effects linear model: filterByExpr on the group factor, TMM scaling factors, voom precision weights, and a ~condition design with control set explicitly as the reference so a positive log2 fold change means higher in cases. A Wilcoxon rank-sum test on log-CPM plus a label-permutation null run alongside it, as the recommended control at this sample size; disagreement between the two is reported, not hidden.

The counts come from salmon as a gene-level table and the profile does not state whether the length correction was applied. No per-sample quant.sf files and no average-transcript-length table are present in the inputs, so the model is fitted on the counts as delivered with no length offset. tximport is not run on a gene table. The consequence — a shift in isoform usage can present as differential expression — is stated in the report rather than assumed away.

For the second half of the question, T1S3 runs treat() against a log2 fold change threshold of 1 (2-fold), giving FDR control for the threshold hypothesis itself; a post-hoc |logFC| filter on a zero-null test would keep the noisiest estimates and control nothing. Both the plain-null set and the threshold-passing set are reported, with the p-value histogram inspected before adjustment as a fit diagnostic, since BH assumes uniform null p-values. Results are sorted by effect size within the significant set, because at n=60 per group the test has power to call fold changes too small to be biologically meaningful. No enrichment step is planned — the question asks for genes and their effect sizes, not pathways.

steps.method: blind VST, PCA on top variable genes, sample distance heatmap
fixed-effects linear model ~condition, reference level control, counts as delivered without length offset
limma-voom with a fixed-effects linear model, plus Wilcoxon rank-sum control
TREAT against a log2 fold change threshold with BH adjustment
Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate with independent filtering

caveats: A large zero-null list with a near-empty threshold list is a legitimate and important result: it means the cohort has power to detect small differences that are unlikely to matter biologically. Report it that way rather than lowering the threshold to produce a longer list.

grounding.reason: No rule covers the report step as such; the settings are taken from the returned report constraints — effect size beside the p-value and sorting by effect size at population scale (R-0089@69f0), the reporting fields (R-0041@059a), and the reproducibility record (R-0086@becf)

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If each group holds 50 or more samples, use limma-voom with a fixed-effects linear model for the differential expression test. In a population cohort the sample-to-sample variation does not obey the negative binomial model, and DESeq2 and edgeR then report many false positives, even on permuted labels. The linear model on the log counts with precision weights keeps the false discovery rate closer to the nominal level than the count models, but it also exceeds it on some data. The paper recommends the Wilcoxon rank-sum test at a large sample size. State this caution in the report, and give the Wilcoxon test or a permutation check as the control.

steps.method: blind VST, PCA on top variable genes, sample distance heatmap
fixed-effects linear model ~condition, reference level control, counts as delivered without length offset
limma-voom with a fixed-effects linear model, plus Wilcoxon rank-sum control
TREAT against a log2 fold change threshold with BH adjustment
